src: 2. Complete each pair of sentences with a word in the box in the correct form.
a) You need to _____ your emotions from the subject matter.
I tried to _____ the cables on the floor.
b) I got _____ by my emotions and overreacted to her words.
The aircraft has been _____. We’ve alerted the authorities.
c) She didn’t feel _____ by her family because they overlooked her efforts.
The theory has been _____ by experimental results.
d) I’m having trouble _____ my thoughts after the call.
Water also provides the means of _____ body temperature.
e) She cracked a joke to _____ tension.
The road was closed while the police tried to _____ the bomb.
f) It was a gut-_____ experience.
They tried to _____ the bag from him but he managed to keep it.
items.why: Complete the sentence pairs using words from a word box in the correct form; this requires typed gap answers and a supporting word bank.

parts.title: Complete each pair of sentences with a word in the box in the correct form.
parts.html:
Слова для перетаскивания: defuse hijacked stabilizing untangle untangling validated wrench wrenched wrenching
a) You need to [untangle] your emotions from the subject matter. I tried to [untangle] the cables on the floor.
b) I got [wrenched] by my emotions and overreacted to her words. The aircraft has been [hijacked]. We’ve alerted the authorities.
c) She didn’t feel [validated] by her family because they overlooked her efforts. The theory has been [validated] by experimental results.
d) I’m having trouble [untangling] my thoughts after the call. Water also provides the means of [stabilizing] body temperature.
e) She cracked a joke to [defuse] tension. The road was closed while the police tried to [defuse] the bomb.
f) It was a gut-[wrenching] experience. They tried to [wrench] the bag from him but he managed to keep it.

items.label: 8. Decide what you might say
src: 8. Decide what you might say in the situations below. Use one of the words or phrases in brackets.
You told your roommate that you are moving out and they got upset. (middle ground, it’s worth, chime)
For what it’s worth, I really enjoyed us living together.
a) You’ve been negotiating a contract with a customer and feel like you have offered a lot but they haven’t been very flexible. (all honesty, disclosure, meet halfway)
b) You and your family went on a camping trip. Your dog broke a leg, your car was stolen and your tent leaked. A friend has now asked you how the trip went. (interject, mildly, in the spirit of)
c) Communicate to a colleague that the strategy she presented might not work. (being honest, middle ground, acknowledge)
d) You want to let a friend know that you understand why they quit their job. (just so, in the spirit of, coming from)
e) You got angry because your friend bailed on you again. He told you not to overreact. (transparency, gently, validate)
f) Your partner has been talking about a problem they have at work. You want to interrupt them to ask about a detail. (gently, chime, acknowledge)

g) You are going to quit your job. You weren’t going to tell your boss until the end of the month but she has now asked you to participate in a big project. Tell her you are quitting. (disclosure, middle ground, it’s worth)
items.why: Speaking task: learners formulate and say responses to situations using the provided phrases.

items.label: Choose an opinion about metaphors
src: 4. Choose an opinion which best describes your attitude to metaphors and explain your choice.

a) “When you're trying to make sense of abstract concepts like the meaning of life, it can be hard to wrap your head around them. But with a good metaphor, it's like a lightbulb goes off and everything just clicks into place.”
b) “I have to be honest – metaphors can be a real pain in the neck. I'd rather stick to plain, straightforward language since any ambiguity or confusion that comes with metaphors can be disastrous.”

c) “I sometimes wonder why some authors are so obsessed with metaphors when keeping the text plain and simple would benefit the book much more. It’s not that I don’t appreciate a good metaphor, but sometimes less is more. Unless it’s poetry, I guess. Poets need metaphors more than prose writers.”

d) “I don't really think about metaphors all that much. I guess they can be useful in marketing or communication, but they're not a game-changer for me. At the end of the day, it's all about results and getting the job done.”
items.why: Learners choose from the provided opinions and explain their choice orally.

items.label: Vrai ou faux ?
src: 4 Écoutez de nouveau. Vrai ou faux ? À l’oral, corrigez les affirmations fausses.
1. Sarah habite dans le quartier des institutions européennes.
2. Sarah trouve que le métro est mieux que le bus.
3. Fatima n’a pas une bonne opinion de la ville.
4. Fatima pense que le soir à Bruxelles est ennuyeux.
5. Pour Léon, la ville de Bruxelles est aussi animée que d’autres capitales européennes.
6. Léon affirme que vivre à Bruxelles est un peu stressant.
5 Lisez la transcription des interviews et répondez.
Aujourd’hui, Radio Bruxelles nous fait voyager au cœur de la ville.
Écoutons la voix de quelques Bruxellois.

Sarah Bonjour, moi, c’est Sarah. J’habite à Bruxelles depuis toujours. C’est une jolie ville, agréable, internationale, surtout dans le quartier des institutions européennes. J’habite à quelques minutes à pied de la Grand-Place, dans une petite rue. Mes voisins viennent des quatre coins de l’Europe : de Grèce, du Portugal, des Pays-Bas… Je prends le métro pour aller au lycée : c’est plus rapide et pratique que le bus.

Fatima Je m’appelle Fatima. Je viens de Paris, j’ai longtemps habité aux États-Unis et au Canada. Je suis arrivée à Bruxelles il y a deux ans. C’est vrai, Bruxelles n’est pas aussi grande que Paris, il n’y a pas autant d’attractions, mais c’est tout de même une capitale, active et accueillante. J’habite dans un quartier très tranquille. Il y a une belle ambiance, on peut faire de longues promenades et les gens discutent beaucoup. Le soir, c’est très animé surtout à côté du célèbre Manneken Pis.

Léon Moi, c’est Léon et je suis né ici. Pour mon travail, je voyage beaucoup : au Brésil, en Chine, et même en Ouzbékistan, mais je reste très attaché à Bruxelles. C’est une ville chaleureuse et dynamique ; et même si elle est moins grande que d’autres capitales, on s’amuse autant. Et on est moins stressé ! La ville offre beaucoup de surprises et d’émotions : on ne s’ennuie jamais !
